newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serb-Moslem tension mounts in northern Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Serb-Moslem tension mounts in northern Bosnia.

text.p: Tensions rose in a sensitive area of northern Bosnia where Serb police arrested three Moslem villagers and used automatic weapons to threaten a United States peacekeeping officer on Friday, a NATO spokesman said.
The incident occurred in the disputed village of Jusici after houses were blown up there overnight, according to local officials.
Western officials later said all three Moslem men were released.

Witnesses said angry Moslem women armed with sticks and bottles had surrounded Russian peacekeeping troops at their communications truck and refused to let them go until the arrested Moslems were freed.
NATO spokesman Major Simon Haselock said only three Russians were surrounded and they had not felt in danger. He said peacekeeping troops had cordoned off the village.
Jusici is one of several flashpoint villages in the Serb sector of the demilitarised zone along the wartime front line.
A series of explosions on Thursday in two other villages in the area wrecked seven houses, including one being rebuilt for Moslem returnees by the United Nations refugee agency.
Haselock said the U.S. officer had been threatened by Serbs carrying long-barrelled weapons in "serious breach" of the Bosnian peace settlement.

A member of the International Police Task Force, charged with helping to bring peace to Bosnia, said the Moslems had been arrested while they went with peacekeeping troops to inspect the blown up houses in Jusici.

Up to 10 Bosnian Serb police armed with illegally-held automatic weapons took the three Moslem villagers to the nearby town of Zvornik. Serb sources said the police had found Moslem- held arms in the village.
Bosnian Serb interior minister Dragan Kijac accused Moslems of having attacked the Serb police when they arrived in Jusici.
NATO said it had "heightened security throughout the troubled area and is preparing for further operations".
Nekir Islamovic, the mayor of Jusici, threatened to kill the Russian soldiers unless the Serbs released their Moslem prisoners.
"I will personally kill all the Russian soldiers if our people don't come back," he said.

Moslem villagers first returned to Jusici last month as part of the Bosnian peace process, but Russian peacekeeping troops discovered they were carrying arms banned under the December 1995 Dayton peace accord for Bosnia.

Serb police are entitled to patrol the villages, but this has stoked up tensions with d the blowing up of houses in the area was clearly an attempt by the Serbs to prevent the Moslems from returning to the villages they lost during Bosnia's 43 months of war.
